questions.text: The Barcelona Pavilion (1929) is the quintessential expression of Mies van der Rohe's spatial philosophy. What structural and spatial elements define it?

options.text: Cruciform steel columns and freestanding planes of onyx, travertine, and glass creating a flowing spatial sequence
Reinforced concrete pilotis supporting a free plan of non-structural partitions inside a cubic white volume
Exposed color-coded mechanical systems on the building exterior with a steel truss roof structure
A parametrically generated concrete shell enclosing a continuously differentiated fluid interior space

rationale.summary: The Barcelona Pavilion uses cruciform steel columns and freestanding planes of onyx, travertine, and glass.

common_misconceptions: Le Corbusier uses a concrete column grid (Dom-ino); Mies uses steel cruciform columns with freestanding planes

questions.text: Which Mies van der Rohe building best exemplifies his concept of 'Universal Space' — a large, column-free, flexible interior volume?

questions.text: The LEA presents a question confusing Mies's 'free-flowing plan' with Le Corbusier's 'plan libre.' What correctly distinguishes these two approaches?

rationale.summary: Corbusier's plan is free to rearrange partitions within a column grid; Mies's plan flows through freestanding planes.
